The Battle of Cabala (379 BC) was fought in Cabala on the island of Sicily during the Sicilian Wars between Syracuse, led by Dionysius I, and Carthage led by Mago II. Syracuse won the battle, and Mago was killed along with 10,000 Carthaginian men; a further 5,000 were taken prisoner. The Carthaginians sued for peace and Mago was replaced by his son, Mago III, who extended the peace by a few days. During that extended period he trained his survivors, and the Battle of Cronium occurred when the peace was over. The exact location of Cabala is unknown, although it is assumed to be in eastern or central Sicily.
Prelude
Dionysius I, tyrant of Syracuse was looking for an excuse to have a war with Carthage, and decided to use the fact that some of the costal Sicilian cities under Carthaginian rule were willing to revolt. He decided to make alliances with some of the rebellious cities. The Carthaginians saw this and sent ambassadors to Syracuse to ask for their cities back, however, they were ignored. Angered by this, Carthage made an alliance with the Italiotes of southern Italy, who were already at war with Syracuse. Mago II, Shofet of Carthage, then recruited a large number of young soldiers from their own populace, and raised money to hire a large number of foreign mercenaries. Next they set sail to Sicily and Italy with a combined force of roughly 25,000 men, including somewhere from 1,000-3,000 cavalry and 6,000-9,000 light armed footmen, looking to fight a two fronted war. The Syracusians also split their forces, with one portion fighting Mago's forces and the other waging war against the Italiotes. After a few minor battles in Sicily and a march inland, what was described as an "important pitched battle" by Diodorus Siculus, was fought on the island between the Carthaginian forces and roughly 20,000 Syracusian and mercenaries including about 15,000 hoplites, 3,500 light footmen, and 1,500 cavalry. Although the exact location is unknown, it is assumed to be in eastern or central Sicily.
Battle
The exact details of the course of the battle are unknown. However, it is known that it was a decisive victory for Syracuse with over 10,000 Carthaginians killed, and a minimum of 5,000 captured. The Carthaginian survivors were forced to retreat to a fortified hill top, that had no access to water. They then fought again, where the Carthaginian Shofet was killed along with others.
Aftermath
Then, the Carthaginian forces sent a delegation to sue for peace. However, Dionysius decided that the only way he would accept was if Mago's forces retreated from the cities of Sicily and paid the cost of the war. These terms was considered to be to harsh by the Carthaginians. They faked satisfaction with the terms, but responded that they were unable to surrender the cities, and that that power lied with their government, they requested a truce for a few days. When Dionysius agreed the truce took effect, Dionysius hoped that he would then take over all of Sicily. Meanwhile, the Carthaginians held a funeral for their leader, and replaced him with his son, Mago III, as well as collecting their dead. The new leader made excuses to extend the peace by a few days. He spent the period of the truce training his troops, in preparation for a future battle. When the truce ended, both sides deployed their armies and began a battle, the Battle of Cronium, in which Mago destroyed the Syracusian army, leaving 14,000 dead.
